note: The living city's rules as data: one file read by the viewer (docs/city/core.mjs) and the Python core (smc.city.rules). Amounts are in whole currency units (Credits, a placeholder currency at par with the US dollar so real-world figures read as they are). Every figure says where it comes from; 'approx.' marks a figure taken as representative where the exact schedule varies by place or could not be confirmed.

clock.basis: the city keeps San Francisco's own time, as the sky does: a day in the city is a day

jurisdictions.basis: approx. city limits as boxes [west, south, east, north]; the county where no city box holds the point

income.basis: single filer. Federal: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (tax year 2026). California: FTB 2025 schedule (the latest published; indexed each year) and the 1% Behavioral Health Services tax over 1,000,000.

payroll.basis: employee shares, 2026: Social Security 6.2% to the wage base (SSA), Medicare 1.45% and 0.9% more over 200,000 (IRS), California SDI on all wages (EDD; approx. 1.3% for 2026)

sales.basis: combined state, county and district rates (CDTFA); approx. where a city's district taxes changed during the year

property.basis: Proposition 13: 1% of assessed value, plus each area's voter-approved debt and parcel levies; the assessed value is the price paid, raised at most 2% a year. Totals approx. (secured roll 2025-26).

transfer.basis: paid by the seller when real estate changes hands. Every county: the documentary transfer tax, 1.10 per 1,000. Cities add their own: San Francisco's whole-value tiers (Business and Tax Regulations Code art. 12-C, as of 2024); Oakland's tiers (Measure X); approx. elsewhere.

vehicle.basis: California: vehicle license fee 0.65% of value a year (DMV), registration and CHP fees, and the transportation improvement fee by value (approx. 2026)

fuel.basis: per US gallon: California excise 61.2c (July 2025 - June 2026), federal excise 18.4c, sales tax on the rest; price before taxes approx.

local.basis: San Francisco: parking tax 25% of off-street parking (Business and Tax Regulations Code art. 9); hotel tax 14%

tolls.basis: Bay Area Toll Authority's seven bridges: 8.50 for a two-axle car from 1 January 2026 (BATA 2026 toll increase), taken one way only; carpools of three or more with a FasTrak CAV tag pay half on weekdays 5-10 and 15-19 (approx.). Golden Gate Bridge: southbound only, set by its district (approx. FasTrak 9.75, invoice 10.75). Without FasTrak an invoice is mailed, due in 21 days; unpaid, a violation notice adds a penalty, then a second.

managed_lanes.basis: lanes from OpenStreetMap (hov:lanes, hov:minimum, hov:conditional, toll:hov; scripts/build_managed_lanes.py). Carpool lanes: two or more (or as signed) in the hours posted. Express lanes (Bay Area Express Lanes, VTA, 101 Express): solo drivers pay a price set by congestion, shown at the entrance; carpools free or half with a FasTrak Flex set to their size. Driving solo in a carpool lane is a violation of at least 490 with penalty assessments (California Vehicle Code 21655.5).

enforcement.basis: San Francisco's automated speed cameras (2025 pilot): 50 for 11-15 mph over, 100 for 16-25, 200 for 26 and over, 500 at 100 mph or faster; parking citations approx. SFMTA schedule

witness.basis: a moving violation (speeding, a carpool lane short of its riders) is charged only where it is seen: in the field of view of one of the map's enforcement cameras (the speed cameras drawn on their poles; each looks along its street, a 70-degree cone out to 45 m, approx. a fixed camera's working range), or with a patrol car within 60 m

vehicles.basis: new prices approx. 2026 California list (the vision's new economy car: 22,000); used by age so a five-year-old hatchback is the vision's 8,000; fuel use EPA combined

water.basis: salinity in practical salinity units (about grams of salt a kilogram); density from UNESCO's equation of state at 15 C, simplified: 999.1 + 0.77 x salinity kg/m3. Corrosion relative to fresh water, after typical carbon-steel loss rates. Bay zones approx. after USGS San Francisco Bay salinity surveys.

zones.basis: San Pablo Bay (approx. 20 in the dry season, much fresher after rain)
the South Bay's former salt ponds, from the map's outlines where named
South Bay below the San Mateo Bridge (approx. 26)

jobs.basis: occupations by workplace; pay an hour on the V2 vision's scale: a basic job pays 120 every 10 minutes of active work (720 an hour, the floor), and every other role keeps its ratio to San Francisco's minimum wage (19.18 from 1 July 2025) in the BLS OEWS 2024 hourly medians for San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont. Shifts as such places keep them.

density.basis: how busy the streets are beyond the residents' own days: passers-by to a 150 m square of streets at the busiest hour, and a multiplier on them and on through traffic -- by default, and in the hotspots (the busiest wins). The Marina is the test district: Chestnut and Union Streets, the Marina Green and the Palace of Fine Arts. Nobody is made up where you look (docs/city/fleet.mjs): the residents are each home's, and the through traffic is a fleet of visitors' cars -- so many to a place of the district by how busy it is, each coming through 4 to 9 times a day from the edge of the streets (a through trip, or about half the time a stop: parked near a shop and an hour or so on foot about the shops) -- sized so the Marina's streets carry the traffic of a busy neighbourhood street (approx.: a busy neighbourhood shopping street carries several thousand to fifteen thousand vehicles a day).

routine.basis: a 24-hour day around each person's shift: sleep, getting ready, the commute, a break mid-shift, errands and meals out, an evening out for some, home and sleep

repair.basis: what breaks (a window, a door, a shopfront) stays broken for half a day, is boarded over with plywood planks, and is back as it was within three days (approx. a glazier's or carpenter's turnaround for a city repair); not yet triggered by anything that breaks

vitals.basis: three bars from 0 to 100. Stamina runs down through the waking day and with effort (sprinting, a shift at work, a workout) and comes back at night, faster asleep at home or in a hotel; food and drink give it back. Health wears down slowly, quickly with no stamina left, and comes back with medicine, a doctor's visit and nights asleep; at none you faint, wake at home and are billed for the ambulance. Strength fades a little each day; workouts at a gym build it, and walking a little. Strength sets how much you can carry. Time away is lived as days are: awake by day, asleep at home by night.

items.basis: what the city's shops sell, on the V2 vision's price scale (a simple meal 35, clothing 100-500). kind is the sales-tax class (groceries and prescriptions are exempt in California). kg is what it weighs to carry; a service is used where it is bought. use is what it does to the bars when used.

stores.basis: what each kind of store sells, by the kinds the map's tenants are (OpenStreetMap shop and amenity tags, and for clinics and gyms the tenant's name). A building with several tenants has a store for each.

handling.basis: how things are picked up, held, thrown and swung, and how high you jump. Lifting: one object up to 12 kg + 0.6 kg a point of strength (24 kg at 20, 72 kg at 100; untrained adults lift about a third of their weight from the floor, trained ones their own weight). Throwing: the arm gives 40-220 J by strength (an untrained throw of a 0.15 kg ball is about 25 m/s, 45 J), capped at 14-30 m/s for light things; under 3 m/s it is no throw. Swinging: rigid things up to 30% of what you can lift, the blow's energy by mass and length. Jumping: the legs push over 42% of their length (53% of height) with 1.6-3.0 body weights by strength (untrained to athletic: 0.3 to 0.8 m), against body and load (approx., after published sports-science figures). material_of, hold and length_m on each item say what it is made of, how it is held (hand, two_hands, shoulder, tool) and how long it is.

found.basis: things left on the pavement to pick up, a few a district each day, where they fall by a seed of the district and the day

transit.basis: the V2 vision's bus trip (15, paid boarding); taxis metered from the flag drop, by the kilometre (approx.)

delivery.basis: a delivery gig: a parcel from a restaurant, café or shop to a home 200 to 900 m away, paid when handed over, half pay if late; gig pay is not withheld from

business.basis: the V2 vision's leases (a storefront 3,000 a week), for the business layer to come

real_estate.basis: price a square metre of floor by use, at real 2025-26 San Francisco levels (homes about 1,000 a square foot; the housing market's neighbourhood prices refine a home's), scaled by county. The vision's own scale (a plot 40,000) was replaced by real prices at the user's direction; Credits stay at par with the dollar.

tools.basis: a strike's energy: a person's swing of each tool at a typical strength (a framing hammer about 40-60 J, a sledgehammer 300-500 J, a punch 20-40 J; approx., after published impact measurements), scaled by strength from 0.6 at none to 1.4 at full. Against each material the strike counts by how the tool works on it (a saw cuts wood, it does nothing to steel). An object breaks when the energy it has taken reaches its catalogue break_energy_j (docs/object-catalogue.json); a blow far below that counts for less than its share, as a tap does not fell a post.

blunt.name: A blow with what you hold

damage.basis: what breaking a thing costs: the city's public works repair it after a while, and breaking what is not yours is vandalism (California Penal Code 594: a fine, and restitution of the repair). Repair costs approx. 2025 Bay Area contractor prices.

work_tasks.basis: a shift is work: tasks come every minute or so, each done where it is (at the counter, at the kerb, in the back) by walking there and pressing V. Pay is for the time worked, as long as some work was done in each ten minutes; three ten-minute stretches with nothing done and you are sent home. Tips are on top (approx. a few credits a customer).

barista: Serve the customer at the counter
Pull a shot and steam the milk
baker: Pull a tray from the oven
Box a cake for a customer
cook: Take the trash out to the kerb
bartender: Change a keg in the back
Card a customer at the door
parking_attendant: Collect a fee at a car
Direct a car to a space
janitor: Empty the bins at the kerb

errands.basis: a neighbour's errand: buy what they ask at the shops it is sold in and bring it to their door. Paid on the doorstep: what you spent back, and a fee by the distance (approx. a gig-app errand's rate).

transit_lines.basis: buses on the real routes (SFMTA GTFS stops, docs/transit-stops.json): each route's stops in the district, in order along it, joined by the streets; a bus every few minutes each way, stopping at each stop to let people on and off. Headways approx. Muni's frequent network (6-12 minutes).

npc.basis: residents without a car on a trip too far to walk: some take a taxi (approx. a third of such trips in San Francisco's TNC-era surveys), others the bus where one line serves both ends

housing.basis: the homes for sale and to rent, mirroring the market: every residential building's type from its OpenStreetMap tag (house, detached and the like are single-family; apartments and residential are multi-unit, split into units by floor area), a share of each type listed at a time as in San Francisco's market (approx. 2025: about 1% of single-family homes and well under 1% of condos for sale; about 3% of apartments advertised for rent), and prices by square foot and neighbourhood (approx. 2025 medians from public listing-site neighbourhood reports; not a valuation of any real home). The listings turn over each week.

mortgage.basis: a 30-year fixed loan (approx. 6.3%, late 2025), 20% down, closing costs 2% of the price; a payment every 30 days; three missed and the bank forecloses

lease.basis: a month's rent ahead and a month's deposit; rent every 30 days; two missed and the landlord evicts

harm.basis: what a blow or a car does to someone, and a crash to a car. A person on foot hit by a car is hurt by the impact speed (approx., after the pedestrian injury-risk curves of Rosen and Sander 2009 and the AAA Foundation's 2011 study: few serious injuries under 10 mph, most over 25 mph); a blow by its energy (rules.json tools: a punch 20-40 J, a sledgehammer 300-500 J). Each band names the injuries it can be; the kind is recorded with the person, its effects (a limp, a cast) are for a later round. Hospital bills approx. 2025 California emergency charges before insurance. A battery is California Penal Code 242/243(a): a fine of up to $2,000. Cars: the share of condition an impact takes by its speed (a 10 mph bump dents, 25 mph wrecks), towed from where it stopped and repaired at a body shop (approx. 2025 Bay Area rates).

online_store.basis: the city's online store: anything a shop in the city sells, bought from wherever you are and brought to you by courier within the minute, at twice the average in-person price (the convenience premium of app delivery is approx. 1.3-2x after fees and markups; the city's is the top of that). Services (a doctor's visit, a haircut), prescription medicine and a shop's own counter meals are not sold online.

tasks.basis: the task board: work posted round the city, each a few steps with a place to go and a thing to do there, and pay on finishing. Courier pay is the delivery gig's (pickup and drop-off both counted); the Presidio's forestry is the Presidio Trust's removal of dead and hazard trees in its historic forest (a dead, dry 8 cm pole felled in a few dozen axe strokes), paid approx. at day-labour rates; the sightseeing pass is the Marina's own visitors' walk.

forestry.name: Presidio forestry: fell three dead trees

initiatives.basis: a party's world is governed by the NPC administration until a full council can be elected (vision: mayor and five seats); meanwhile its residents may put measures to a vote of the party, within the platform's limits

toll_carpool_share.label: carpool share of the bridge toll
